gaps.lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

gaps.lead: There's a rumour that the factory will close.
She started working here five years ago.
gaps.explanation: 'Started five years ago' → present perfect with 'for'.

gaps.lead: 'I have never lied to the press,' the minister said.
gaps.explanation: deny + -ing (ever strengthens the denial): denied ever lying.

gaps.lead: I'd love to be lying on a beach right now.
gaps.sentence: I ___ lying on a beach right now.
gaps.explanation: wish + past subjunctive: I wish I were (formal 'were', not 'was').

gaps.lead: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
A committee is looking into the sudden rise in food allergies.
gaps.sentence: The sudden rise in food allergies ___ a committee.
gaps.hint: phrasal verb in the progressive passive
gaps.explanation: 'A committee is looking into X' becomes the passive 'X is being looked into by a committee'.
